analysis:
Examined all supplied test source, patches and file metadata against the indexed model and selected TB-002/TB-011 details. DoctorOperatorDiagnosisTests.swift:95-136 adds blocked/authorized traffic diagnostics; StatusCommandRunTests.swift:121-178 tests missing status, keychain refusal and authorization output. These use synthetic daemon state and sandboxed CLI execution; they do not themselves grant serving permission or change billing, encryption, credential custody or inference isolation. No concrete security regression is established in these changes.
ServingReadinessTests.swift:38-145 tests advisory eligibility, expiry, legacy compatibility, disconnection, local Apple-call failures and state serialization. Lines 151-191 test unauthorized-connection recovery: idle-only threshold, first-attempt jitter, exponential backoff and recognized coordinator verdicts. These expectations are relevant to T-052, T-053, T-057 and T-058 but are not proof of production enforcement or live policy.
Integration must examine ServingReadiness, UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery and their changed CLI/provider-loop callers: ensure displayed eligibility remains advisory, stale status is cleared or bound to each connection, and reconnects preserve endpoint-resumption ceilings, revocation and current coordinator authorization. Verify that recovery's busy check protects active inference/draining and that actual scheduling preserves tested backoff rather than resetting it on each registration. Those implementations are outside this batch; missing evidence is a coverage limit, not an observed missing control. Existing machine-ID display, usage warnings and runtime guard tests are unchanged.
